claims.text: Poss CVA: neuroimaging and bedside glucose are mandatory.
claims.quote: Although diagnosis is clinical, neuroimaging and bedside glucose testing are mandatory.

claims.text: CT or MRI first to exclude intracerebral hemorrhage, subdural or epidural hematoma, or a tumor.
claims.quote: Neuroimaging with CT or MRI is performed first to exclude intracerebral hemorrhage, subdural or epidural hematoma, and a rapidly growing, bleeding, or suddenly symptomatic tumor.

claims.text: Sus lrg vessel occlusion: CTA or MRA, esp w.in 24 hrs of onset.
claims.quote: Guidelines recommend that all patients with clinical suspicion of large vessel occlusion should undergo vessel imaging (CTA or MRA), especially within 24 hours of symptom onset given advances in acute stroke treatment.

claims.text: CVA bloods: CBC, met panel, PT/PTT, fasting glucose, A1C and lipids.
claims.quote: Routine blood testing typically includes complete blood count (CBC), metabolic panel, prothrombin time/partial thromboplastin time (PT/PTT), fasting blood glucose, hemoglobin A1C, and lipid profile.

claims.text: Sudden or severe weakness or any resp Sx: forced vital capacity and maximal inspir force; VC < 15 mL/kg or inspir force < 20 cm H2O means higher risk of ventilatory failure.
claims.quote: If sudden or severe true general weakness or any respiratory symptoms are present, forced vital capacity and maximal inspiratory force must be tested to assess risk of acute ventilatory failure. Patients with vital capacity < 15 mL/kg or inspiratory force < 20 cm H2O are at increased risk.

claims.text: Routine labs are USU done unless the cause = obvious: CBC, lytes w calcium and magnesium, glucose, kidney and liver tests, TSH, ESR, hepatitis C serology.
claims.quote: Unless the cause is obvious, routine laboratory tests (CBC, electrolytes [including calcium and magnesium], glucose, kidney and liver function tests, TSH, ESR, hepatitis C serologic testing) are usually done.

claims.text: Brain UMN signs: MRI (CT if MRI isn't poss).
claims.quote: If brain upper motor neuron dysfunction is suspected, the key test is MRI. CT is used when MRI testing is not possible (eg, in patients with an older, non-MRI compatible cardiac pacemaker).
If myelopathy is suspected, MRI can detect lesions in the spinal cord.

claims.text: Neuropathy, myopathy or neuromusc junction dx: EMG and n. conduction studies.
claims.quote: If polyneuropathies, myopathies, or neuromuscular junction disorders are suspected, the key tests that help differentiate these mechanisms of weakness are electrodiagnostic testing (electromyography and nerve conduction studies).

claims.text: Even when acute, these studies help separate GBS, botulism and other neuromusc junction disorders.
claims.quote: However, these studies can help differentiate among certain acute disorders, such as acute demyelinating neuropathy (eg, Guillain-Barré syndrome), acute botulism, and other acute neuromuscular junction disorders.

claims.text: Poss myasthenia gravis: ice pack test and acetylcholine-r antibodies.
claims.quote: If findings suggest myasthenia gravis, an ice pack test and serologic testing (eg, acetylcholine receptor antibody levels, sometimes anti–muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibodies)
